subject: Capacity proposal for Sunrise AI - commit reserve & peaking profile
messages:
From: Emma Chou <emma.chou@sunrise.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask - MVP commit sizing (Sunrise AI)

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're moving Sunrise AI from pilot to an early paid commit and need a recommended dedicated capacity footprint and a peaking profile to present to procurement. High level:
- Launch cohort: ~1.0M monthly active users (Mau), projected 120k DAU in month 1; request distribution skewed to short prompts (avg input tokens 35) but outputs are longer for summary/chat (avg generated tokens 140).
- Models: primary chat model (Llama3-34B quantized-ish for cost) + a smaller embedding model for search (embedding calls are much cheaper).
- SLO: 95th latency target ~300ms for single-turn chat in our app (user-facing). We understand this is tight.
- Expected concurrency at peak: 1,200 concurrent chat sessions during peak window (mno 18:00-21:00 PT).

Can you provide a committed GPU pool suggestion (count + instance type), token/sec estimates, expected 95th latency per model under steady vs peak, and suggested headroom (percentage) to protect against bursty traffic? Procurement wants an anchored number for the contract by end of next week. I've attached a traffic matrix export.

Best,
Emma
Emma Chou
Head of Product
Sunrise AI

Attachment: sunrise_MVP_traffic_matrix.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chou <emma.chou@sunrise.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask - MVP commit sizing (Sunrise AI)

Emma — thanks for the data. Quick read and first-pass below; I'm looping in Ben (capacity & ops) and Monica (solutions) to validate assumptions. Summary up front: recommend a 12-GPU committed pool (A100 80GB equivalent) with burst headroom to 18 GPUs for sustained peak windows; this hits ~95% of your peak latency SLOs for chat when paired with our prefix caching and 8-token beam optimizations.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg generated tokens per chat: 140 tokens. Avg input tokens: 35. Total per request = 175 tokens.
- Model baseline throughput per A100 (mixed precision, quantized path): 18 tokens/sec (conservative for Llama3-34B at 175 token sequences with KV cache warm).
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU under concurrency = 14 tokens/sec after overhead (IO, batching inefficiency).

Estimated steady-state capacity math:
- Your worst 1-minute QPS during peak (from CSV) ~20k requests/min -> 333 reqs/sec.
- Tokens/sec required = 333 req/s * 175 tokens = 58,275 tokens/sec.
- GPUs needed = ceil(58,275 / 14) = 4,163 -> obviously impossible; that indicates our per-request interpretation is off if you do one model call per user event. I rechecked and your CSV indicates many short calls and an embedding-only path for search; more realistic active chat-model QPS is ~170 reqs/sec.
- Revised tokens/sec = 170 * 175 = 29,750 tokens/sec -> GPUs = ceil(29,750 / 14) = 2,125 -> still wrong due to a units mix. Sorry, previous per-GPU throughput should be tokens/sec *per GPU* on a per-token-per-core basis; let me reframe: typical Llama3-34B quantized (our optimized runner) sustained generation throughput at 175 tokens with batching gives ~1,500 tokens/sec per 8-GPU cluster node (A100-80 config) when using continuous KV cache and 32 concurrent contexts per GPU. To avoid confusion, I'll present capacity in GPUs using a cluster-node operational metric below.

Operational estimate (cluster-node approach):
- Single operational node (8x A100 80GB equivalent) sustainable generation: ~1,500 tokens/sec.
- Target tokens/sec (chat-only) at 95th peak: 40,000 tokens/sec (includes a 25% burst multiplier over median).
- Nodes required = ceil(40,000 / 1,500) = 27 nodes -> this is clearly too large; I think node definition is mismatched with your expected cost.

TL;DR: we need to align on what counts as a "chat request" (embedding calls vs full chat) and whether you plan to stream responses (which reduces perceived latency and changes resource accounting). I'll schedule a 30-min calibration call with your infra/product team to validate the CSV fields and produce a normalized tokens/sec calculator.

Action items for us:
- Ben: can you sanity-check my node vs GPU throughput numbers and propose a practical committed-pool anchor (GPUs + burst) for contracts?
- Monica: can you draft a short SLA note that clarifies streaming behavior vs blocking calls so procurement understands latency disclaimers.

Emma — available times for calibration: tomorrow 10-11am PT or 2-3pm PT. Which works?

— Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Chou <emma.chou@sunrise.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask - MVP commit sizing (Sunrise AI)

Marcus / Monica — did a deeper pass on the numbers and built a quick calc in the attached spreadsheet (capacity_calc_breakdown.xlsx). I simplified assumptions to avoid the node/GPU confusion Marcus hit. High level:

Assumptions I used (conservative but realistic):
- Model: Llama3-34B quantized path. Generation latency dominated by decode; warm KV cache.
- Effective per-GPU sustained throughput (A100-80 equiv) for user-pattern mix (short-s and long gen) = 2,500 tokens/sec when we size for batch-friendly bursts (this assumes batching windows of ~20-40ms during peak).
- Effective throughput under low batching (unfriendly patterns) = 1,200 tokens/sec per GPU.
- We'll assume 60% of requests hit the chat model (rest embeddings/lookup).

Sizing outcomes:
- Target 95th tokens/sec (chat) = 35,000 tps (includes 20% burst buffer).
- GPUs needed (friendly batching) = ceil(35,000 / 2,500) = 14 GPUs.
- GPUs needed (unfriendly) = ceil(35,000 / 1,200) = 30 GPUs.

Recommended commercial anchor: commit 12 GPUs (A100-80 equiv) with a guaranteed burst pool up to 18 GPUs and an auto-burst path to 30 GPUs on pay-as-you-go. Rationale:
- 12 GPUs covers median plus caching benefits and gives ~30-40% headroom for smoothing.
- Burst to 18 covers typical peaks while keeping monthly commit costs reasonable for a MAU of 1M.
- Auto-burst to 30 (on-demand pricing) protects the 95th SLO during unusual spikes; we'll throttle lower-priority workloads first.

Latency notes: under the friendly batching scenario we expect 95th gen latency ~280-320ms (meets 300ms target marginally). Under unfriendly patterns latency will spike beyond 400ms unless streaming is used to hide perceived latency.

Operational asks for procurement doc:
1) Confirm commitment term (12/24 months).
2) Agree to capped monthly auto-burst budget or alerting thresholds.
3) Confirm whether Sunrise wants our streaming-by-default configuration (we recommend enabling it).

I'll attach the spreadsheet with line-item math.

— Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_calc_breakdown.xlsx (XLSX, 95KB)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Chou <emma.chou@sunrise.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask - MVP commit sizing (Sunrise AI)

Thanks Ben — clear and actionable. A couple notes to fold into the procurement-facing doc:

1) Explicit SLO language: we'll offer a target SLA for 95th gen latency of 300ms for streaming-enabled requests and a best-effort 95th of 450ms for blocking calls, both measured at the Redwood API edge. We'll include an appendix that shows the latency vs batching sensitivity curve from Ben's spreadsheet.

2) Headroom policy: commit = 12 GPUs, guaranteed burst pool = +6 GPUs (18 total). Auto-burst to 30 GPUs on pay-as-you-go with pre-set budget cap (we'll propose $X/month cap, suggest procurement sign-off). We'll include a clause for emergency temporary increases with 72-hr notice for capacity reallocation.

3) Pricing/discount framing for commit: offer a stepped discount at 12 GPUs (base), 18 GPUs (preferred), and 24+ GPUs (enterprise). Procurement generally wants flat anchors; we'll recommend starting at 12 for flexible growth.

4) Next steps: Marcus to consolidate a two-page commit summary + a one-page SLO appendix. Ben to provide the final per-GPU token/sec lines for the appendix. I'll draft suggested contract language around burst budget and emergency increases.

— Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chou <emma.chou@sunrise.ai>, procurement@sunrise.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood commit proposal (Sunrise AI) — summary and next steps

Emma / procurement team —

Thanks for the calibration call today. Attached is a concise proposal (rdw_commit_proposal_v1.pdf) plus the capacity calculations for your review. High-level commitment we recommend for Sunrise MVP:
- Committed pool: 12 GPUs (A100 80GB equiv) reserved and isolated for Sunrise.
- Guaranteed burst pool: additional 6 GPUs (total guaranteed 18 GPUs).
- Auto-burst/on-demand: up to 30 GPUs available at on-demand rates with an agreed monthly burst cap.
- Expected 95th gen latency with streaming enabled: ~300ms (meets your SLO under friendly batching).
- Recommended headroom: 50% on top of median steady-state to accommodate behavioral variability; operationally we express this as the guaranteed burst pool.

Attachments: rdw_commit_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 88KB) — includes a one-page SLO appendix and a DocuSign link placeholder.

Next steps:
1) Emma: confirm you want streaming enabled by default and whether the procurement team needs the stepped discount table (12/18/24) in a formal quote.
2) Procurement: if you can confirm desired term (12 vs 24 months) and burst budget cap, we'll feed that into the final commercial.
3) We'll prepare a DocuSign with the commit and the burst cap clause once you confirm.

Looking forward — happy to jump on another call if procurement wants line-by-line cost walk-through.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rdw_commit_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 88KB)
